intro: You're looking for the best commercial mortgage near you, which usually means you want a broker who understands business lending and can find a deal that fits your plans. Commercial mortgages fund the purchase or refinance of business premises or investment property, and the right broker can guide you through the process. We introduce you to a suitable UK mortgage broker who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a commercial mortgage broker usually need
need_lead: Most people searching for the best commercial mortgage near me are business owners or investors who need funding for a property and want expert help to navigate the commercial lending market.
needs: You are buying business premises, such as a shop, office, or warehouse, and need a mortgage to complete the purchase.
You want to refinance an existing commercial mortgage to get better terms or release equity for other business purposes.
You are an investor looking to purchase a commercial property as an investment and need a mortgage to fund it.
You have been turned down by your bank and need a broker who can approach other lenders that may be more flexible.
You are unsure how much deposit you need or how lenders will assess your business and the property, and want clear guidance.
context_heading: Understanding commercial mortgages and finding the best broker for you
context: Commercial mortgages are not like residential ones: lenders assess both the business and the property, deposits are usually larger, and most commercial lending is unregulated. That means you have fewer consumer protections, so it's important to choose a broker who is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) for any regulated advice they give. You can check a broker's status on the FCA register.

When searching for the best commercial mortgage near me, it's wise to speak to a few brokers and compare what they offer. Ask whether they search the whole market or a limited panel, and how they are paid—by lender commission, a fee, or both. That way you can judge for yourself which broker is best for your situation.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: The type of property you are looking to buy or refinance, such as a shop, office, warehouse, or investment property.
The approximate purchase price or value of the property, and how much deposit or equity you have available.
Whether you are buying for your own business use or as an investment to let out.
Any details about your business, such as how long it has been trading and its annual turnover.
Whether you have already approached lenders or had a mortgage application declined.
Any specific requirements, such as a fast completion or a particular type of commercial mortgage.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the mortgage broker
questions: Are you authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, and can you provide your firm reference number?
Do you search the whole of the market or a limited panel of lenders?
How are you paid for your services—by lender commission, a fee, or both?
What deposit will I need for a commercial mortgage, and how will lenders assess my business?
What documents will I need to provide for a commercial mortgage application?
What happens if my application is declined—can you help me find alternative lenders?

faqs.a: Most commercial lending is unregulated, which means you have fewer protections than with a residential mortgage. However, mortgage advice is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), so any broker you use should be authorised or an appointed representative, and you can check this on the FCA register.

faqs.q: How much deposit do I need for a commercial mortgage?
faqs.a: Deposits for commercial mortgages are usually larger than for residential mortgages, but the exact amount depends on the lender and the property. A broker can explain what different lenders typically require for your situation.

faqs.q: Can I get a commercial mortgage if my business is new?
faqs.a: Some lenders are more flexible than others, and a broker can help you find lenders who are willing to consider newer businesses. Be prepared to provide a solid business plan and financial projections.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a whole-of-market and a limited-panel broker?
faqs.a: A whole-of-market broker searches across many lenders, while a limited-panel broker only has access to a selected group. Brokers must tell you which type they are, so you can decide what suits you best.

extra_heading: Judging the best commercial mortgage near you
extra: When you search for the best commercial mortgage near me, the word best is doing a lot of work. There is no single best commercial mortgage, because what suits a shop purchase will not suit an investor refinancing a let property, so the useful question is which deal fits your business and the property it is secured on. A broker near you can talk through how lenders look at the business and the property together, and what deposit they are likely to expect.

Being near you matters less than being easy to reach and clear to deal with. Commercial lending is mostly unregulated, so the usual consumer protections are thinner, but mortgage advice itself is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). Check that the broker is authorised, or an appointed representative of an authorised firm, on the FCA register, and ask whether they search the whole market or a limited panel and how they are paid, whether by lender commission, a fee, or both.

At a first appointment, expect questions about the property, your deposit or equity, how the business trades and what you plan to do with the premises. A good broker will explain the trade-offs rather than promise the cheapest deal, and will tell you plainly if your plans look difficult for lenders. That conversation, more than any label, is how you judge who is best for you.

extra_faqs.q: Does 'near me' mean I should only use a broker in my town?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. What matters is that the broker understands commercial lending and is easy for you to speak to, whether that is face to face or by phone. Many business owners work with a broker further away if the fit is better.

extra_faqs.q: Can a broker promise me the best or cheapest commercial mortgage?
extra_faqs.a: No, and you should be wary of anyone who does. Commercial lending is mostly unregulated and terms depend on the lender's view of your business and the property, so compare what each broker says about lenders, deposit and fees before deciding.

extra_faqs.q: What if my business has only just started trading?
extra_faqs.a: Some lenders are more open to newer businesses than others, and a broker can explain which are worth approaching. Expect to provide a business plan and financial projections, and be ready to discuss a larger deposit.
